summary: Steel tower on Cannon Mountain, Franconia NH, built 1951 with the tramway; out of service 1981, removed 2007 or 2008; concrete blocks reported in 2010.

facts.design: Four-legged tower, about 35 feet tall; material given as steel (1951) and wood (1959)
facts.status_note: Removed in 2007 (Willhite) or 2008 (Forest Lookouts). Concrete blocks of the four legs were reported in 2010; no source says whether they remain.

access.note: Summit reached by the year-round aerial tram; no tower to climb

visit.trail_note: No tower to climb. The summit is reached by the year-round aerial tram.

events.note: Steel tower built in association with the tramway; first displayed at the Eastern States Exposition
Survey team describes a fire lookout and an observation platform on the summit
Taken out of service; left under the guy wires of the new summit deck and radio-television tower
Removed in the fall because it could not be saved; the Forest Lookouts page gives 2008
Survey reported only the concrete blocks of the four tower legs remained

evidence.supports: Steel tower built in 1951 in association with the tramway
evidence.quote: In 1951, a steel tower was built in association with the Cannon Mountain Tramway.

evidence.supports: Tower first displayed at the Springfield exposition, then moved to the summit
evidence.quote: The steel tower had been on display at the Eastern States Exposition in Springfield MA in 1951, and was removed to the Cannon site after the Exposition closed.

evidence.supports: 1958 survey describes fire lookout and observation platform
evidence.quote: In 1958, a survey team described both a fire lookout and an observation platform on the summit.

evidence.supports: 1959 description: about 35 feet, wood, four legs
evidence.quote: They said the tower was about 35 feet tall constructed of wood and supported by four legs.

evidence.supports: Taken out of service in 1981 and left under the guy wires of the new summit deck
evidence.quote: In 1981, it was removed from service and was tucked under the guy wires of the new summit observation deck and radio-television tower.

evidence.supports: Removed in fall 2007 because it could not be saved
evidence.quote: In 2007, the tower was removed in the fall because it had deteriorated to the point where it could not be saved.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page gives removal as 2008
2010 report: only the concrete blocks of the four legs remained
evidence.quote: only the concrete blocks of the four tower legs remained.

evidence.supports: Aerial tram runs year round to the summit
evidence.quote: the current tram today still runs the 2.1 mile journey year round to the summit offering scenic views to tourists.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the tower as gone
Blog list marks the mountain as standing, with no detail

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite says the tower came down in the fall of 2007; the Forest Lookouts page says 2008. Both are shown, and the event uses 2007.
Willhite calls the 1951 tower steel, but its 1959 description says wood on four legs. The record shows both and does not pick one.
The Hike Over the Hill list marks the mountain as standing with no detail; the FFLA list and Willhite's history say the tower is gone.

sources.title: You Are Here: NH Fire Towers

notes_for_editor: The 1951 build date, the steel-or-wood conflict and the 1958-2010 history all rest on one page, WillhiteWeb, an Appalachian Trail hobby site; it is the only source for the build. The removal year conflicts (2007 vs 2008). The Hike Over the Hill 'Standing' entry is unverified and probably refers to summit structures, so the story only notes it. The cannonmt.com history lists a 1939 'Lookout' addition that may or may not be this tower, so it is not used. The Taxpayers for Cannon history page failed on certificate checks. The 2010 concrete-blocks report is the last source on the site itself; nothing says whether the blocks remain today.
